coverageArticles.headline: Trump administration planning to reimburse doctors treating vaccine ‘injury’
coverageArticles.description: Experts warn that sweeping changes elevate health secretary RFK Jr’s anti-vaccine agenda and personal profit The Trump administration is finalizing a rule to reimburse doctors who diagnose, treat and counsel patients with side effects from vaccines in what experts believe is an attempt to undermine trust in vaccines and to create an evidence base on their purported risks.

coverageArticles.headline: Meet the short seller that flagged Nvidia’s ‘significant China problem’ six months ago—including ‘uncomfortably close’ ties with Alice Huang
coverageArticles.description: Six months ago, Nvidia stock peaked at $235.74 a share. But while others were focused on the AI boom and Nvidia’s growing market cap, one research firm saw a China-sized crack in the foundation. Now, Nvidia is down 27.9% since then, and Jensen Huang has been ousted as CEO following his romantic affair with a suspected Chinese spy.

coverageArticles.headline: Nvidia had no succession plan when Jensen Huang quit. Former Fortune 500 CEOs call it ‘preposterous’
coverageArticles.description: Nvidia’s total lack of the settled succession plan that’s a cornerstone of all well-run companies exposed a shocking weakness in its corporate governance. That’s the view of three former Fortune 500 CEOs, and a leading consultant, whom Fortune interviewed on arguably the most consequential leadership earthquake ever to rock the business world.

coverageArticles.headline: Megaspeed says Alice Huang left in 2025 as it launches internal probe into reports about its business
coverageArticles.description: The Singapore-based cloud computing company has faced heightened scrutiny since reports linked Nvidia's Jensen Huang to former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang.

coverageArticles.headline: ‘Jensen Huang lost his mind’: how AI’s smartest man fell for the world’s oldest trick
coverageArticles.description: Jensen Huang’s affair with a suspected spy is Silicon Valley’s worst nightmare come true

coverageArticles.headline: How travelers can navigate trips as ground stop effects linger, expert says

coverageArticles.description: The Hollywood Reporter had a prime seat for the once-in-a-lifetime event on a Southwest plan — which took off about an hour before all planes were grounded by the FAA — that also featured The Used and Lolo.

coverageArticles.headline: Ground Stop Highlights Chronic Vulnerabilities in Air Traffic System
coverageArticles.description: The Federal Aviation Administration’s aging air traffic control infrastructure has had several disruptive failures in recent months, as officials have sought to make upgrades.

coverageArticles.description: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy points blame toward contractor in explaining Friday's nation-wide aviation ground stop.

coverageArticles.headline: Trump Kept Out of Sight as F.A.A. Issued Flight Ground Stop
coverageArticles.description: The F.A.A. called a rare halt on flights nationwide, but the president stayed away from cameras and issued social media posts on the entertainment industry and California’s Democratic governor.

coverageArticles.headline: Elon Musk, other tech execs sign petition calling on Nvidia to reinstate Jensen Huang
coverageArticles.description: The petition had attracted more than 115,000 signatures as of Saturday afternoon.

coverageArticles.headline: Tech Leaders Rally Behind Jensen Huang
coverageArticles.description: In social media posts and letters to Nvidia’s board, Mr. Huang’s billionaire peers described him as a singular leader who could not be replaced at Nvidia.

coverageArticles.headline: How Some Flights Were Exempt From the Ground Stop
coverageArticles.description: Dozens of international flights departed from the United States during Friday’s nationwide ground stop. Some planes also left for Hawaii from the West Coast.

coverageArticles.description: Hoobastank, Simple Plan and more bands on their way to Vans Warped Tour performed mid-flight on Nov. 13 during the nationwide grounding.

coverageArticles.headline: Aviation industry expert on next steps after "everything went haywire" with huge ground stop
coverageArticles.description: Travel industry analyst Harvey Harteveldt shares his perspective following a nationwide FAA ground stop.

coverageArticles.headline: How to get a refund after the massive FAA ground stop
coverageArticles.description: Frustrated travelers are still dealing with delays and cancellations after a nationwide ground stop. Points Path CEO Julian Kheel shares his advice for passengers looking to protect their money when travel plans go awry.

coverageArticles.headline: Pilot, former air traffic controller react to national ground stop
coverageArticles.description: Travelers are still facing delays and cancellations after a national FAA ground stop was lifted. Commercial airline pilot Captain Laura Einsetler and former air traffic controller Todd Yeary share their reactions.

coverageArticles.headline: Hoobastank, Simple Plan Play Mid-Flight Concert Aboard Warped Tour-Bound Plane
coverageArticles.description: Warped Tour-bound artists Hoobastank and Simple Plan performed a mid-flight concert Friday, a gig that coincided with a nationwide air travel shutdown.

coverageArticles.headline: What to know about flights after the U.S. nationwide ground stop
coverageArticles.description: The longest flight stoppage in 25 years ended around 8:15 p.m. ET Friday, allowing some domestic flights to take off from U.S. airports. Officials expected a full recovery by Sunday.

coverageArticles.headline: Work to replace old copper wire led to the FAA’s ground stop
coverageArticles.description: A view of an information board at the Chicago O'Hare International Airport, filled with waiting passengers on November 13, 2026. | Anadolu via Getty Images At a press conference today, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said that Friday's nationwide ground stop ordered by the FAA was related to work replacing outdated copper wire with a fiber optic line at a "remote FAA facility."

coverageArticles.headline: Nvidia board urged to consider 'potential return of Jensen Huang' by two major investors
coverageArticles.description: Two Nvidia investors with about $2.13 billion of stock disclosed as of June 30 are calling for a deliberate leadership search after Huang’s resignation.

coverageArticles.headline: FAA blames Friday's ground stop on 'equipment issue' during telecoms network upgrade
coverageArticles.description: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said initial investigations pointed to an issue with contractor L3Harris updating old tech at a remote location.

coverageArticles.headline: FAA ground stop throws college football into chaos, while the NFL is safe
coverageArticles.description: After flights were halted for more than four hours Friday, several teams across multiple sports had their plans affected.

coverageArticles.headline: Updated start times for college football games affected by FAA ground stop, broken down by conference
coverageArticles.description: Although the FAA ground stop was resolved within hours, its ripple effects forced college football game time changes across the Big 12, SEC, and Big Ten.

coverageArticles.headline: Asian governments react to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s exit
coverageArticles.description: Some governments moved to confirm chip supply commitments, while others are monitoring the impact on local projects or addressing ongoing investigations.

coverageArticles.headline: Thousands of flights canceled as airlines work to recover from nationwide ground stop
coverageArticles.description: The nationwide stop was the first since January 2023, when another key Federal Aviation Administration computer system that sends notices to pilots malfunctioned, and the second since the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks.

coverageArticles.headline: What to Know About Friday’s Nationwide Ground Stop
coverageArticles.description: The air traffic control system’s overloaded, antiquated telecommunications equipment sustained its latest widespread failure, prompting a call for more money to fuel faster upgrades.

coverageArticles.description: Thousands of flights still canceled as officials blamed ageing air control system for nationwide grounding

coverageArticles.headline: FAA ground stop puts obstacle in front of social media stars trying to get to AEW's Full Gear PPV
coverageArticles.description: College football, NHL, NBA and even pro wrestling were affected Friday when the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) issued a nationwide ground stop, causing chaos and confusion around the U.S. Social media star "Big Boom" A.J. was set to be one-half of a tag team with Q.T.

coverageArticles.headline: Jensen Huang and the decline of the visionary showman founder CEO
coverageArticles.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang at CES 2025 in Las Vegas, Nevada, on January 6, 2025. | Photo by Artur Widak/NurPhoto via Getty Images On January 6th, 2025, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang got his rockstar moment at last.

coverageArticles.headline: 3,000 flights cancelled as FAA ground stop chaos stretches into 2nd day
coverageArticles.description: The chaos from the FAA's nationwide ground stop lingered into early Saturday morning, with thousands of flights cancelled as airlines played catch-up. Why it matters: Millions of travelers will find themselves inconvenienced over what the government says was simply old technology that couldn't keep up with modern upgrades. Driving the news: As of 5:15 a.m.

coverageArticles.headline: Flight disruptions continue after FAA lifts ground stop, some college football games delayed
coverageArticles.description: U.S. flights are resuming after the FAA ground stop, but delays and cancellations are still piling up.

coverageArticles.headline: Thousands of flights canceled or delayed Saturday after FAA’s nationwide ground stop
coverageArticles.description: Atlanta, Chicago O’Hare and New York’s JFK were among the hardest-hit airports as airlines worked to get planes and crews back into position.
coverageArticles.headlineAuthor: Corky Siemaszko, Tom Costello, Joy Y. Wang, Marlene Lenthang

coverageArticles.headline: How to Land 4,000 Planes During a Ground Stop
coverageArticles.description: For four and a half hours, the sky above the United States emptied out. Normally, throughout the day and the night, thousands of planes are taking off, crisscrossing the country, and landing.

coverageArticles.headline: Scenes From the Nationwide Ground Stop
coverageArticles.description: On Friday afternoon, the Federal Aviation Administration issued a rare ground stop at all U.S. airports, citing “extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety.” Across the country, departing flights were held for hours before the stop—attributed to a telecommunications outage—was lifted, disrupting travel plans for some 1.5 million people.

coverageArticles.headline: FAA ends hours-long nationwide ground stop
coverageArticles.description: The FAA lifted its nationwide ground stop Friday night after hours of chaos and thousands of delays and cancellations. Why it matters: The effects of the rare and extreme move will likely ripple through the weekend, with travelers stranded and airlines' planes and crews out of position.

coverageArticles.headline: Duffy details timeline of ground stop, demands more FAA funding
coverageArticles.description: Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy gives the timeline of the paralyzing FAA ground stop, which left travelers across the country stranded for hours. Duffy says the issue was due to old communications systems.

coverageArticles.headline: Of Course Americans Blamed the Ground Stop on AI
coverageArticles.description: For many hours, the Federal Aviation Administration did not explain why it issued a national ground stop in the United States this afternoon. The agency described the cause only as a “ telecommunications outage ” and cited “ extraordinary circumstances ,” but failed to say more. So speculation abounded: Was the problem connected with the onboarding of a new AI route-selection system this week?

coverageArticles.headline: Airport Chaos Began Long Before the Ground Stop
coverageArticles.description: Every civilian airplane in the United States has been told not to fly, owing to a nationwide FAA ground stop. As I write this, very little is known about the nature of the safety risk or the issue underlying it.

coverageArticles.headline: Stranded passenger in Las Vegas on nationwide ground stop: "Nobody has answers"
coverageArticles.description: Clara Pablo was trying to get home from Las Vegas to New York on Friday when the FAA issued a nationwide ground stop. She joined CBS News' to share her experience. Then, CBS Atlanta's Nakell Williams reports on the scene from Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport.

coverageArticles.headline: FAA issues rare nationwide ground stop due to 'extraordinary circumstances'
coverageArticles.description: Air travel across the country came to a standstill on Friday after the Federal Aviation Administration issued a rare nationwide ground stop citing “extraordinary circumstances” and “reasons of safety.” Aviation correspondent Miles O’Brien reports.

coverageArticles.headline: Update to network connecting air traffic control system led to outage before ground stop, sources ay
coverageArticles.description: An update to the private communications network that connects America's air traffic control system caused the system to reboot, leading to a crash and a communications outage, multiple sources told CBS News. Lindsey Reiser anchors continuing coverage.

coverageArticles.headline: Flight Canceled During the FAA Ground Stop? Here’s What to Do.
coverageArticles.description: Travelers are entitled to a refund if your flight is canceled, regardless of the reason, or if a flight is significantly delayed or changed and you decide not to take it.

coverageArticles.headline: FAA has lifted its third-ever nationwide ground stop
coverageArticles.description: Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy blamed obsolete equipment for the outage.

coverageArticles.headline: Some international flights allowed to depart U.S. amid FAA ground stop
coverageArticles.description: Some flights headed to other countries are being permitted to depart from the U.S. amid Friday's nationwide ground stop. Major Garrett anchored ongoing coverage.

coverageArticles.headline: FAA lifts rare nationwide ground stop
coverageArticles.description: The Trump administration said the issue was due to hardware in the US air-traffic control systems.

coverageArticles.headline: Some airports beginning to run out of space for planes amid nationwide ground stop
coverageArticles.description: A source with knowledge of the situation told NBC News that Reagan National Airport is at capacity and that Chicago O’Hare is nearing capacity, meaning there is no place for planes to park and that some of the planes may have to divert to other airports.

coverageArticles.headline: No indication of nefarious attack before FAA ground stop, Mullin says
coverageArticles.description: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin said Friday's FAA ground stop was caused by a telecommunications outage and there is currently no indication of a nefarious attack. Major Garrett anchors ongoing coverage.

coverageArticles.headline: DHS head Markwayne Mullin says there is not a threat to the U.S. amid FAA ground stop
coverageArticles.description: Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin spoke to at the White House on Friday afternoon after the FAA issues a total ground stop. NPR was there for the briefing.

coverageArticles.headline: Stuck on the tarmac without information: Travelers share their ground stop experiences
coverageArticles.description: Passengers stuck on airplanes on tarmacs across the country during the FAA ground stop on Friday share their stories.

coverageArticles.headline: Secy. Mullin says FAA ground stop was caused by 'telecommunication outage'
coverageArticles.description: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told reporters the nationwide ground stop issued by the Federal Aviation Administration was the result of a telecommunication outage. He also assured that the issue was the result of some for of attack or hack.
